B: Which ribosomal site contains the normal stop codon immediately before release?
E site
A site
P site
Exit tunnel
The A site is the decoding site; the completed chain is esterified to the P-site tRNA. The E site accommodates discharged tRNA, and the exit tunnel carries the nascent chain.
Which triplet is ordinarily a termination signal in the standard code?
UGG
UAC
UGA
AUG
UGA is a standard stop, whereas UGG encodes tryptophan, UAC tyrosine and AUG methionine. Certain organelles and specialized recoding contexts are exceptions.
A bacterial mRNA ends with UAG. Which class I release factor normally recognizes this triplet?
RF1
RF2
RF3
RRF
RF1 recognizes UAG and UAA. RF2 recognizes UGA and UAA. RF3 promotes factor turnover, and RRF acts during recycling.
Which bacterial stop signal is recognized by either RF1 or RF2?
UAG
UGA
UGG
UAA
UAA lies in both recognition classes. UAG is normally RF1-specific and UGA RF2-specific. UGG is a sense codon.
Which factor recognizes all three standard stops during eukaryotic cytosolic translation?
eEF2
eRF1
eRF3
eIF3
eRF1 carries out stop recognition and supports peptide release. eRF3 is an accessory GTPase; eEF2 is a translocase and eIF3 participates in initiation and associated recycling functions.
What is directly hydrolyzed during normal peptide release?
An internal peptide bond
A phosphodiester bond in mRNA
The peptidyl-tRNA ester linkage
The stop codon
Hydrolysis separates the chain from its P-site tRNA and preserves its amino acid sequence. Neither the mRNA backbone nor an internal peptide bond is the intended substrate.
Which conserved motif is associated with class I release-factor hydrolytic activity?
GGQ
CCA
AUG
Walker A alone
GGQ is part of the release factor's catalytic domain. CCA is the tRNA terminus and AUG a codon; a nucleotide-binding motif alone does not identify the class I hydrolytic function.
What is the role of water in the normal termination reaction?
It charges the incoming tRNA
It creates a new peptide bond
It removes the stop codon
It participates in ester hydrolysis
Water replaces the elongation reaction's incoming amino group as the relevant reacting species, releasing the chain. It does not charge tRNA or cleave the messenger.
Which bacterial protein promotes turnover of class I release factors?
IF1
RF3
RRF
EF-Tu
RF3 is a GTPase that facilitates RF1/RF2 departure. RRF is a recycling factor, IF1 an initiation factor, and EF-Tu delivers aminoacyl-tRNA.
Which factor pair primarily promotes bacterial posttermination subunit splitting?
RF1 and RF2
IF1 and IF2
RRF and EF-G
EF-Tu and EF-Ts
RRF and EF-G act on the posttermination complex. RF1 and RF2 catalyze peptide release; the other pairs primarily support initiation or elongation.
Which is a major role of bacterial IF3 after subunit splitting?
Preventing premature reassociation
Hydrolyzing peptidyl-tRNA
Decoding UGA
Adding the terminal residue
IF3 stabilizes a small-subunit state suitable for initiation by discouraging reassociation. It is not a release factor or an aminoacyl-tRNA delivery factor.
Which eukaryotic factor is an ATPase involved in ribosome recycling?
eRF3
eEF1A
eIF4E
ABCE1
ABCE1 cooperates with eRF1 in posttermination subunit splitting. eRF3 and eEF1A are GTPases; eIF4E binds the cap.
Which statement distinguishes eRF3 from bacterial RF3?
Both directly decode all stops
eRF3 assists productive eRF1-mediated termination; RF3 mainly promotes class I factor turnover
Both are ATP-dependent ribosome splitters
Neither binds nucleotide
The names do not imply identical positions in the cycle. Both are GTPases, not class I stop decoders or ATP-dependent splitters.
What is a polysome?
A complex of ribosomal proteins without RNA
A single ribosome translating several separate mRNAs at once
Multiple ribosomes associated with one mRNA
Several proteins sharing one peptide bond
A polysome consists of more than one ribosome on a shared messenger. Each ribosome normally translates its own chain.
For a uniform polysome translating one ORF, which nascent chain tends to be longest?
The one closest to the normal stop
The one closest to the initiation codon
All must be identical in length
The one outside the cell
Translation proceeds toward the 3′ end while the chain grows N to C. A ribosome farther along the ORF generally carries a longer chain, provided it has not released or undergone unusual processing.
What does a polysome profile primarily measure?
Exact protein synthesis flux at each codon
DNA replication rate
Absolute enzyme catalytic activity
Distribution of sedimenting ribosomal complexes
Gradient absorbance reflects sedimentation and RNA-rich particles; protein output requires an additional flux measurement. Positional occupancy requires another method.
Which treatment can destabilize ribosomal subunit association through Mg²⁺ chelation?
Addition of a sense codon
EDTA
Addition of methionine
Replacement of UAG by UAA
EDTA removes available divalent cations, which can destabilize ribosomes. It is a useful dissociation control but is not a physiological recycling factor.
What is a stop-loss mutation?
A sense codon replaced by an earlier stop
A change of one normal stop to another
A normal stop replaced by a sense codon
Deletion of the ribosome
A stop-loss permits extension until another usable stop or an abnormal message end. A sense-to-stop change is a nonsense mutation; a stop-to-stop change preserves the standard amino acid sequence.
Which observation best distinguishes peptide release from recycling?
Direct detection of the chain's covalent attachment to tRNA
A change in DNA concentration alone
Counting mitochondria
Measuring only total cell size
A retained peptidyl-tRNA linkage indicates that the chemical release step has not completed. Recycling can fail after the chain is already free; the other measurements are not stage-specific.
Which statement about a normal stop codon is correct?
It must lie at the physical 3′ end of RNA
It always destroys mRNA
It directly encodes water
It is interpreted in the selected reading frame
A stop must occupy the decoding position in the active frame. A 3′ untranslated region can remain after it, and the message is not routinely destroyed by normal termination.
Which statement about a nonsense suppressor tRNA is correct?
It cannot carry an amino acid
It can compete with termination and introduce an amino acid at a stop
It always restores the original amino acid
It is identical to RF1
The suppressor may deliver an amino acid through altered decoding. Its charging identity determines which residue is inserted, so full length does not guarantee restored activity.
A mature eukaryotic mRNA has a single coding sequence but six associated translating ribosomes. It is:
Polycistronic but not polysomal
Neither monocistronic nor polysomal
Monocistronic and polysomal
Necessarily bacterial
Cistron number describes coding regions, while polysomal status describes ribosomal occupancy. A single-ORF eukaryotic message can carry multiple ribosomes.
What is normally preserved during physiological ribosome recycling?
Intact functional ribosomal subunits
A permanent covalent link between mRNA and peptide
All intersubunit contacts indefinitely
Only the stop codon
Subunit association is reset without routine degradation of rRNA and ribosomal proteins. The nascent chain was previously freed and the RNA can be reused.
Which example is a legitimate exception to standard cytosolic UGA termination?
UGA always encodes glycine
UGA is the usual bacterial initiation codon
UGA is a DNA polymerase recognition site
UGA can encode tryptophan in vertebrate mitochondria
Genetic-code assignments can differ among compartments. The vertebrate mitochondrial code assigns UGA to tryptophan; this does not invalidate the standard cytosolic code.
What is the best interpretation of a stalled ribosome on a truncated message without a stop?
Normal RF1-dependent UAG recognition is guaranteed
A rescue pathway may be required
The ribosome has automatically finished a correct full-length protein
The RNA is necessarily still being transcribed
The absence of a properly positioned termination codon can prevent normal release. Rescue addresses abnormal states and need not produce the intended full-length chain.
A 120-residue chain before processing contains how many peptide bonds?
A linear chain of n residues contains n−1 peptide bonds. The terminal ester to tRNA is a different bond, and a stop contributes no residue.
Which event occurs after peptide release in the canonical eukaryotic cycle?
ABCE1-assisted subunit splitting
Initial selection of AUG for that same chain
Charging of its last amino acid for the first time
Transcription of its first codon
The ATP-dependent recycling apparatus dismantles the posttermination complex. Initiation and aminoacylation precede chain completion; transcription is a different process.
Why can normal protein output fall after a recycling defect?
The genetic code must change in every transcript
All peptide bonds are hydrolyzed
Every mRNA becomes polycistronic
Reusable subunits become sequestered
Posttermination complexes tie up ribosomes that would otherwise initiate on other messages. This indirect resource limitation does not require widespread sequence changes.
AR: Assertion: UAA can be decoded by either bacterial class I release factor. Reason: RF1 recognizes UAA/UAG and RF2 recognizes UAA/UGA.
Both statements are true and the overlapping specificity directly explains the assertion.
Assertion: a larger polysome signal proves greater protein output. Reason: longer ribosome residence time can raise mean occupancy.
The assertion is false and the reason true. A slowed departure rate can increase occupancy even when output is unchanged or lower.
Assertion: the terminal ester is cleaved during normal termination. Reason: the final sense codon is selected in the translation reading frame.
Both are true, but reading-frame selection alone does not explain ester hydrolysis; release-factor-mediated chemistry does.
Assertion: bacterial RF3 is a class I stop decoder. Reason: RF3 contains the stop-specific GGQ catalytic function of RF1.
Both are false. RF3 is a class II GTPase and does not substitute for the recognition and hydrolytic activity of RF1 or RF2.
Assertion: eukaryotic recycling uses an ATP-dependent factor. Reason: ABCE1 acts with posttermination eRF1 to promote subunit splitting.
Both are true; ABCE1 supplies the ATP-dependent recycling activity described.
MS: Choose the correct statements: I. UAG is recognized by bacterial RF1. II. UGA is recognized by bacterial RF2. III. RF3 adds glutamine at a stop. IV. UAA can be recognized by both class I factors.
I, II and IV describe canonical specificity. III confuses the release-factor GGQ motif with an incorporated amino acid.

Choose the correct statements: I. A normal stop is exposed in the A site. II. The completed chain is carried by the P-site tRNA before release. III. A peptide bond must be cleaved to remove the final amino acid. IV. Recycling follows release.
III is incorrect: the linkage to tRNA is an ester, not an internal peptide bond.
Choose the correct statements: I. RF3 is a GTPase. II. eRF3 is a GTPase. III. ABCE1 is an ATPase. IV. RRF is a stop-decoding tRNA.
The first three statements identify nucleotide-dependent factors correctly. RRF is a protein recycling factor.

Choose the correct statements: I. A polysome can form on a monocistronic RNA. II. Polysomes can occur on ER-associated messages. III. Svedberg coefficients add arithmetically. IV. Heavy fractions necessarily prove fast elongation.
I and II are correct. Sedimentation coefficients depend on more than mass, and heavy occupancy is not proof of fast elongation.
M: Match 1 RF1, 2 RF2, 3 RRF, 4 eRF1 with a recognizes all three cytosolic eukaryotic stops, b recognizes UAA/UAG in bacteria, c recognizes UAA/UGA in bacteria, d bacterial posttermination recycling.
RF1 and RF2 have overlapping specificity; RRF acts after release; eRF1 recognizes the three standard eukaryotic stops.
Match 1 nonsense mutation, 2 stop-loss mutation, 3 polysome, 4 ABCE1 with a multiple ribosomes per message, b premature stop, c ATP-dependent eukaryotic recycling, d extension beyond the former stop.
A nonsense mutation introduces a stop; a stop-loss removes it. Polysome describes occupancy and ABCE1 participates in recycling.
C: A standard-code ORF normally makes 420 residues. Codon 116 becomes UAG. A suppressor allows readthrough in 8% of 500 otherwise productive initiation events; all resulting chains are stable. How many short and full-length chains are expected, and how long is the short product?
460 short of 115 residues; 40 full-length
460 short of 116 residues; 40 full-length
40 short of 115 residues; 460 full-length
500 short of 116 residues

0.08 × 500 = 40 readthrough products and 460 ordinary premature-release products. The stop replaces residue 116, so the short chain has 115 residues. The full-length sequence may contain a substituted amino acid.
A bacterial reporter shows release yields UAA 80%, UAG 4%, UGA 83%. Wild-type yields approximately 85% at each stop. The test uses preformed pretermination complexes. Which direct defect best fits?
RRF absence
RF2 loss
RF1 impairment
IF3 hyperactivity
Selective loss at UAG indicates RF1 impairment. RF2 can support UAA and UGA; RRF and IF3 act primarily after release and are not expected to produce this stop-specific single-round pattern.
A mutant eRF1 binds a pretermination complex at normal frequency but the fraction of covalently attached peptide remains high. Which hypothesis is most directly supported?
The RNA has no stop codon
Defective hydrolytic domain or its accommodation
Enhanced aminoacylation
Increased ABCE1-mediated splitting

Binding with retention of the ester points toward a defect after recognition, such as the GGQ-containing domain or its proper placement. Additional structural or mutational evidence is needed to localize the defect precisely.
A bacterial mutant releases peptide at normal rates in a single-round assay but 70S posttermination complexes containing uncharged tRNA accumulate. Which test is most informative?
Measure DNA GC content
Replace every stop with AUG
Measure charged tRNA abundance only
Test whether RRF/EF-G restore subunit splitting

The chemical release step has succeeded, so a direct recycling assay and factor complementation address the observed defect. DNA composition, stop replacement and global charging are not specific to the trapped posttermination state.

A 301-residue ORF is translated at 10 residues/s after the first residue is in place. Included nonelongation dwell is 6 s, and a new ribosome enters every 6 s. Under independent steady flow, what are mean occupancy and output?
6 ribosomes; 10 chains/min
10 ribosomes; 6 chains/min
36 ribosomes; 6 chains/min
5 ribosomes; 60 chains/min
Residence is (301−1)/10 + 6 = 36 s. Entry rate is 1/6 s⁻¹, so N = 6 and J = 10 min⁻¹ if all finish. Occupancy and output have different units.
In the same model, elongation slows to 5 residues/s with entry unchanged and no crowding. What follows?
Occupancy stays 6 and output doubles
Occupancy becomes 11 and output stays 10/min
Occupancy becomes 3 and output halves
Both occupancy and output become 11/min
T = 300/5 + 6 = 66 s; N = 66/6 = 11. Output remains equal to successful entry at 10/min under the specified no-crowding assumptions. Real congestion could reduce entry.
A treatment doubles mean ribosome occupancy on a message but halves full-length protein production per minute. Which conclusion is justified without further data?
Initiation necessarily doubled
The message must have doubled in length
Occupancy and flux diverge; slower transit or failed completion is plausible
All ribosomes are now translating twice as fast
Occupancy alone cannot resolve entry, transit and completion probability. A slower exit or reduced completion can yield this pattern; several alternatives require tests.

For a 151-residue bacterial chain, a model counts 2 phosphate equivalents per aminoacylation, two GTP per added residue after initiation, one initiation GTP, one RF3 GTP and one recycling GTP. What is the total?
Charging gives 2 × 151 = 302; elongation gives 2 × 150 = 300; additional specified transitions give 3. Total 605 equivalents. ATP molecule count is 151, not 605.
An idealized coding segment is 1,200 nt and minimum center-to-center ribosome spacing is 40 nt. Ignoring boundary effects, what is the approximate packing bound?
1,200/40 = 30 particles. This is a rough geometric bound, not a prediction of physiological occupancy.
At a stop site, competing first-order rates are termination 4.5 s⁻¹ and readthrough 0.5 s⁻¹. What is readthrough probability?
The competing-exit model gives 0.5/(4.5+0.5)=0.10. The absolute readthrough rate cannot be interpreted as a probability without including the competing termination rate.
A mutant halves k_t from 4.5 to 2.25 s⁻¹ without changing k_r = 0.5 s⁻¹. What is the new modeled readthrough probability?
0.5/(2.25+0.5)=0.1818, or about 18.2%. The rate reduction changes competition; it does not necessarily double the fraction exactly.
A stable mRNA receives ribosomes at 0.25 s⁻¹; 80% complete a full-length chain. What is the expected output per minute?
J = q a = 0.8 × 0.25 = 0.2 s⁻¹; multiplying by 60 gives 12/min. Total entry is 15/min, not all of which is productive.
A drug blocks new initiation while elongation and termination continue. A 600-residue message takes approximately 60 s to traverse. What pattern is most consistent?
Polysomes progressively run off over roughly a minute
Every polysome instantly becomes larger
A permanent increase of all heavy peaks is mandatory
All mRNA is immediately destroyed
Existing ribosomes can complete and leave; no new ones replace them. The actual disappearance time depends on position, elongation rates and stop dwell, so the 60 s estimate is approximate.
A dual-reporter stop construct shows twice the downstream signal after a treatment. Which additional control best addresses a major alternative explanation?
A measurement of nuclear diameter
A construct/control that tests independent downstream initiation and confirmation of fusion product size
A count of total genomic chromosomes
An unrelated promoter sequence alone
Downstream initiation can mimic readthrough. Fusion-product identity and suitable initiation controls distinguish continuity of translation from a separate event; RNA normalization also matters.

A profile has more 80S particles and fewer polysomes after ABCE1 inhibition. Released full-length peptide from isolated pretermination complexes is normal, but subunit splitting is reduced. Which interpretation is strongest?
eRF1 stop specificity has changed to bacterial RF2 specificity
All 80S particles are active elongating complexes
Posttermination recycling is directly compromised
The result proves transcription increased
The isolated assays identify normal release and impaired splitting. Bulk peaks alone are ambiguous, but the biochemical stage-specific measurements support recycling failure.
In a simple eukaryotic comparison, pretermination complexes with GTP analogue recruit eRF1/eRF3 but release peptide slowly; authentic GTP supports rapid release. What does this show most directly?
GTP is incorporated into the final peptide
ABCE1 uses only GTP
Water is unnecessary for peptide release
Normal nucleotide-cycle progression supports efficient termination

The observation supports a role for GTP-dependent rearrangements. It does not identify a direct chemical GTP reactant for ester hydrolysis; analogue effects on binding and conformational equilibria remain possible.
A stop-loss mutation replaces the normal stop by a sense codon. Six downstream sense codons precede the next in-frame stop. How many residues are appended if all are decoded?
The former stop now contributes one residue plus six downstream sense codons. The new stop contributes none.

A bacterial extract releases UAG peptide normally on a single round but loses activity during repeated rounds with limiting RF1. Adding RF1 transiently restores output; adding RRF alone does not. What further hypothesis is worth testing?
Every tRNA synthetase has lost specificity
RF1 turnover, including RF3-dependent departure
The UAG triplet has become UGA in every message
The large subunit is absent from every initial complex

Single-round activity indicates that RF1 recognition and release can occur. Repeated-round failure suggests factor availability or turnover. Direct RF1 residence measurements and RF3 complementation would help distinguish these alternatives.
